summary: Barcode sequences are open and large (BOLD: 20.6 million animal specimens, 462,020 plant specimens), so within- and between-species genetic distances can be computed, and a few single-genus speciation-continuum datasets exist (Drosophila pairs with Nei's D and isolation indices; Heliconius alignments; others). Missing: rank labels at the variety and subspecies end linked to specimens, morphological distance, and any cross-clade table covering the full continuum.
next_step: Check BOLD and GenBank specimen records for subspecies labels, assemble the Drosophila, Heliconius and stickleback datasets as a first multi-clade set, and compute distances before applying rank labels (as the assessors' obstacles require).
obstacles_confirmed: BOLD's summary API reports specimens and BINs, not precomputed pairwise distances.
No single dataset spans variety, subspecies and species pairs for several clades.
The Roux et al. grey-zone data were not found as a repository record in DataCite.
